turns.text: I verified the mobile OTP yesterday while testing, and today selecting the account fails. Nothing else changed.

attachment.name: select-account.txt
attachment.text:
curl -X POST https://abhasbx.abdm.gov.in/abha/api/v3/profile/login/verify/user \
  -H "REQUEST-ID: 3d7e5f2a-8c1b-4a9d-b6e0-4f2c8a1d9e44" \
  -H "TIMESTAMP: 2026-09-29T11:02:09.771Z" \
  -H "T-token: Bearer <MASKED_TOKEN>" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <MASKED_TOKEN>" \
  -d '{"ABHANumber":"<MASKED_ABHA_NUMBER>","txnId":"c8b2e4f1-9a3d-4c7e-8f1b-2d5a6e9c0b55"}'

HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request

{"message":"Invalid T-token"}

must_contain: Invalid T-token means the verify token is wrong or expired: verify the OTP again and use the fresh token
The T-token header carries the short lived token from the login verify call, sent as Bearer <token>; it is not the X-token
The response of this call carries the person's X-token in token, with a refresh token
notes: Diagnose group, attached curl with a stale short lived token: it catches an answer that blames the ABHA number or the gateway session instead of naming the expired T-token and the re-verify fix.
